implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class defines ROWS=6, COLS=7 and builds a 2‑D list of that size.
Game class stores a list of Player objects, tracks _turn_index, and switches turns after each valid move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.get_valid_move() prompts with input() and parses an integer column number.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range and not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: get_valid_move() checks numeric conversion, range, and Board.is_valid_column(); Board.drop_disc() also raises InvalidColumnError and ColumnFullError.
Board.drop_disc() places the disc in the lowest empty cell; Game.play() prints Board.render() after each move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect horizontal, vertical, and diagonal four‑in‑a‑row
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win() iterates over four direction vectors and uses _count_discs to count consecutive discs.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect draw when grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full() returns True when the top row has no EMPTY cells; Game.play() ends with a draw message.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graceful termination on win or draw
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.play() returns after printing a win or draw message.
main.py creates Board, two Player instances, a Game, and calls game.play() under if __name__ == '__main__'.

critical_issues: File columnfullerror.py defines InvalidColumnError and ColumnFullError without importing ConnectFourError, which would raise a NameError if that file were imported. The rest of the code imports the correct definitions from exceptions.py, so the issue does not affect execution but represents dead/buggy code.
The implementation relies on interactive console input, which may hinder automated testing environments.
judge.summary: The submitted source files contain a complete, functional implementation of a standard Connect Four game meeting all core requirements: a 7×6 board, two alternating players, column input with validation, disc placement, win/draw detection, and a runnable entry point. Minor concerns include an unused, broken exception module and the interactive nature of the input, but these do not prevent the core game from executing correctly.
